title: Pandas Time Series Revision Notes
summary: Quick revision of pandas time series: parsing dates with to_datetime, DatetimeIndex, date ranges, resample, rolling windows, shift and pct_change, and time zones. Ends with common mistakes and a cheat sheet.

chapters.title: Datetime Mental Model
points: Pandas stores timestamps as datetime64 (ns in pandas 2; pandas 3 infers us from strings and Python datetimes): Timestamp is a single value, DatetimeIndex is an index of them, Timedelta is a difference between two
Time series work = a DatetimeIndex that is sorted and unique-ish; it unlocks slicing, resample and rolling('7D')
Dates arrive as strings (str dtype in pandas 3, object in older pandas), so parse first: nothing time-aware works on string columns
NaT is the datetime missing value (the NaN of dates); it propagates through arithmetic and is skipped by most aggregations
Naive timestamps have no time zone; aware ones carry tz: mixing the two in ordering comparisons (<, >) or subtraction raises TypeError, while == just returns False

chapters.title: Parsing Dates and Building a DatetimeIndex
points: pd.to_datetime(s) parses strings, ints and lists into datetime64; a Series gives a Series, a list gives a DatetimeIndex
Pass format='%Y-%m-%d' explicitly: faster and removes day/month guessing; %d %m %Y %H %M %S %b %A are the key codes
dayfirst=True for 03/04/2024 meaning 3 April; the default reads it as March 4 (month first)
errors='coerce' turns unparseable values into NaT instead of raising; the default errors='raise' stops on the first bad value
unit='s' or 'ms' converts epoch integers; utc=True parses mixed offsets into one UTC column
df.set_index('date') after parsing, or pd.read_csv(parse_dates=['date'], index_col='date') in one step, makes the DatetimeIndex

chapters.title: Date Ranges and Slicing by Time
points: pd.date_range(start, end, freq='D') builds a fixed-frequency index; give any two of start, end, periods
pd.date_range('2024-01-01', periods=5, freq='W') makes exactly 5 weekly stamps; end is inclusive when given
Frequency aliases: D day, B business day, W week, ME month end, MS month start, h hour, min minute (the old 'M' and 'H' aliases raise ValueError in pandas 3)
Partial string slicing on a sorted DatetimeIndex: df.loc['2024'], df.loc['2024-03'], df.loc['2024-03-01':'2024-03-15'] with both ends inclusive
Index attributes for grouping: idx.year, idx.month, idx.dayofweek (Mon=0), idx.day_name(); df.between_time('09:00','17:00') filters by clock time

chapters.title: Resample, Rolling, Shift and pct_change
points: df.resample('ME').sum() is groupby on time bins: needs a DatetimeIndex (or on='col'); choose the aggregation: sum, mean, last, ohlc
Resample down (daily to monthly) aggregates; resample up (daily to hourly) creates NaN rows, then fill with .ffill(), .bfill() or .interpolate()
df['x'].rolling(7).mean() is a window of 7 rows; rolling('7D') is a window of 7 calendar days and needs a DatetimeIndex
min_periods=1 stops the first window-1 rows from being NaN; expanding().mean() grows from the start, ewm(span=7).mean() weights recent values more
s.shift(1) moves values down a row (lag); shift(-1) pulls the next value up (lead); shift(freq='D') moves the index labels instead of the values
s.pct_change() equals s / s.shift(1) - 1 with the first row NaN; pct_change(periods=7) compares with 7 rows earlier; s.diff() is the absolute change

chapters.title: Time Zones and Common Mistakes
points: tz_localize('Asia/Kolkata') attaches a zone to naive timestamps without changing the wall-clock time; tz_convert('UTC') changes the zone of aware timestamps and keeps the instant
tz_convert on naive data raises TypeError and tz_localize on aware data raises too: localize first, convert after; use tz_localize(None) to strip the zone
Store and compute in UTC, convert to local only for display; daylight saving gaps and repeats need ambiguous='infer' or nonexistent='shift_forward' in tz_localize
shift or rolling on an unsorted index gives wrong results silently (rolling('7D') raises): call sort_index() first; shift(1) across gaps shifts rows, not days, so asfreq('D') first
Comparing a naive column to an aware Timestamp, or leaving dates as strings, are the two most common time series bugs; check df.dtypes and df.index.tz

chapters.title: Time Series Cheat Sheet
points: Parse: pd.to_datetime(s, format=..., errors='coerce', utc=True); read_csv(parse_dates=..., index_col=...)
Build: pd.date_range(start, periods=n, freq='D'); slice df.loc['2024-03']; df.between_time(a, b)
Aggregate by time: df.resample('ME').agg({'sales':'sum','price':'mean'}); upsample then .ffill()
Windows: rolling(7).mean(), rolling('7D').sum(), expanding().max(), ewm(span=7).mean()
Change: shift(1) lag, shift(-1) lead, pct_change() ratio, diff() difference
Zones: tz_localize('Asia/Kolkata') then tz_convert('UTC'); sort_index() and check dtypes before any resample
